title: Log-rate pressure
summary: Write-heavy batches of 3,000-byte rows into demo.log_rate_scratch, each deleted right after it commits, so the table stays small while the log keeps working. The run asks for 2 MB of log per second per intensity level. On Azure SQL Database, more than the service objective's log rate shows up as log-rate governance; on SQL Server it shows up as WRITELOG waits and log flushes. Each run stops after maxLogMb of log, at its deadline, or on a stop request.

concurrency.description: Writer sessions; they share the run's log budget and requested rate.

intensity.description: Requested log rate: 2 MB per second per level (10 MB/s at the default), unthrottled at 10.

notes.T3: The service backs up and truncates the log; the run's maxLogMb budget bounds how much it generates.
notes.T1: Simple recovery: the log truncates at checkpoints and stays under its 8 GB cap.
notes.T2: Simple recovery: the log stays under its 4 GB cap; the runner checks the guest volume first.

maxLogMb.description: Total log to generate across all sessions (an estimate); the run ends early when it's reached.

expectedHubSignals.signal: SqlServerWaitStats: Log Rate Governor wait category (LOG_RATE_GOVERNOR) on T3
SqlServerWaitStats: Tran Log IO (WRITELOG) on T1 and T2
SqlServerPerformanceCountersCommon: Log Bytes Flushed/sec and Log Flushes/sec rising
SqlServerStorageIO: writes on the log file

expectedSymptoms: Write throughput flattens at the service objective's log rate on T3, with sessions waiting on log-rate governance
On SQL Server, sustained log writes and WRITELOG waits
Data size stays flat: every batch is deleted after it commits
queryLevelEvidence: sys.dm_exec_requests wait_type LOG_RATE_GOVERNOR or WRITELOG for ContosoCare.Demo/log-rate-pressure sessions
reset: Auto-cleanup and reset truncate demo.log_rate_scratch; business data is never touched.
